lesson_title: The Headline and the Till Slip
hook_text: Bank X shouts 8,3%. Bank Y whispers 8,1%. Bank Y pays you more. Grade 11 maths teaches you to read the fine print and win.
clip_script: Two banks want your savings. Bank X's window shouts eight comma three percent a year. Bank Y's says eight comma one — but compounded monthly. Everyone picks X, right? Wrong — and the trick is the difference between the headline and the till slip. That poster number is the NOMINAL rate — a headline. The EFFECTIVE rate is the till slip: what your money actually grows by in a full year, fine print included. Print the slip by pushing one rand through the machine. Bank Y slices its eight comma one into twelve little paydays — and every payday's interest starts earning interest immediately. One rand becomes one comma zero-eight-four. That's an effective eight comma four-one percent. Bank X? Pays once a year — its slip reads exactly eight comma three. Y beats X. The quieter poster wins. That's the whole skill: never compare headlines. Convert every offer to its till slip — the effective rate — then compare like with like. Banks bet you'll read the big number and skip the fine print. Grade eleven maths is how you call the bluff.
visual_style: Two rival bank windows glow on a night street; posters flash big percentages while animated till slips print the true rates, coins split into monthly paydays that snowball down the screen, and the underdog bank's slip stamps the win.
pacing: Punchy rivalry setup, slow-motion zoom into the fine print, accelerating payday snowball, mic-drop verdict.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never be fooled by a headline rate again.
